name: go-indep-2
requirements: semver/semver.go: Parse(s string) (Version, error) accepts exactly SemVer 2.0.0 syntax and returns an error for anything else: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH decimal numbers that fit in uint64, then an optional -prerelease and an optional +build, each a dot-separated list of nonempty identifiers made only of ASCII letters, digits and hyphens. Core numbers and all-digit prerelease identifiers have no leading zeros (build identifiers may). Nothing may precede or follow the version, not even spaces. Pre and Build hold the identifiers in order. String() returns MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, then -Pre and +Build joined with dots when nonempty, so it round-trips every valid input. Compare(a, b) returns -1, 0 or 1 by SemVer precedence: core numbers numerically; a version with a prerelease ranks below the same version without one; prerelease identifiers compare left to right, all-digit ones numerically and below any others, others in ASCII byte order; if every shared identifier is equal, the longer list ranks higher. Build metadata never affects Compare. ParseConstraint(s string) (Constraint, error) parses alternatives separated by ||; spaces around || and at either end are ignored; an alternative is one or more comparators separated by spaces, all of which must hold. A comparator is an optional operator (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=, ~ or ^) immediately followed by a version that Parse accepts; no operator means =. A hyphen range A - B (spaces around the hyphen, versions without an operator on both sides) is the two comparators >=A <=B. Operators compare with Compare. ~X.Y.Z means >=X.Y.Z and <X.(Y+1).0. ^X.Y.Z means >=X.Y.Z and <(X+1).0.0, or <0.(Y+1).0 when X is 0, or <0.0.(Z+1) when X and Y are 0. Anything else, including an empty alternative, is an error. Check(v) reports whether any alternative holds, except that a version with a prerelease satisfies an alternative only if one of its comparators names a version with the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and a prerelease. Max(versions, c) returns the highest version that satisfies c, and false when none does. IncMajor, IncMinor and IncPatch return the next version with no prerelease or build: X+1.0.0, X.Y+1.0 and X.Y.Z+1, except that a prerelease already at that level is released instead: X.0.0-pre.IncMajor() is X.0.0, X.Y.0-pre.IncMinor() is X.Y.0, and X.Y.Z-pre.IncPatch() is X.Y.Z. Sort(versions) sorts by Compare and keeps the order of equal versions.

textwrap/textwrap.go: Wrap(text string, width int) []string wraps greedily, counting runes, not bytes. Blank lines (only whitespace) separate paragraphs: leading and trailing blank lines are dropped, and consecutive paragraphs are separated by exactly one "" line. Within a paragraph, words are maximal runs of non-whitespace; whitespace, newlines included, only separates them. Each line takes as many words as fit, joined by single spaces, with no leading or trailing space. A word longer than width starts a new line and is cut into width-rune pieces; its last piece may be followed by more words. Text with no words gives no lines, and width < 1 counts as 1. Fill joins Wrap's lines with \n. Indent(text, prefix string) adds prefix to every line that contains non-whitespace; other lines and all newlines are unchanged. Dedent(text string) removes the longest run of spaces and tabs (compared byte for byte) that starts every line containing non-whitespace, and empties whitespace-only lines while keeping their newlines. Justify(text string, width int) []string returns Wrap's lines, but each line that is not the last of its paragraph and has two or more words is widened to exactly width runes by adding spaces between its words: gap sizes differ by at most one, and the leftmost gaps are the wider ones. Shorten(text string, width int, placeholder string) string collapses every whitespace run to one space and trims the ends; if the result has at most width runes it is returned. Otherwise it returns the most leading words, joined by spaces and followed directly by placeholder, that fit in width runes; if not even one word fits, it returns placeholder without its leading whitespace when that fits, else "". ExpandTabs(text string, tabSize int) string replaces each tab with spaces up to the next column that is a multiple of tabSize, counting columns in runes from the start of each line; tabSize < 1 counts as 1. WrapIndent(text string, width int, first, rest string) []string wraps like Wrap but starts each paragraph's first line with first and its other lines with rest; a prefix counts toward width, leaving at least 1 rune for words, and a long word's pieces fill each line's room. The "" lines between paragraphs get no prefix. Center(line string, width int) string pads line with spaces to width runes, half on each side with any odd space on the right; a line already at least width runes long is unchanged. Table(rows [][]string, gap int) []string aligns cells into left-aligned columns, each as wide in runes as its widest cell, separated by gap spaces (gap < 1 counts as 1); rows may have fewer cells, and trailing spaces are trimmed from every line. Box(text string, width int) []string frames Wrap(text, width-4): with inner the rune count of the longest wrapped line (0 when there are none), the first and last lines are + then inner+2 dashes then +, and each wrapped line, blank ones included, becomes "| " + the line padded with spaces to inner runes + " |".
dependencies: The units share no types, imports or files.
